content:
Maya Chen: Heads-up: rolled INT8 mixed-precision kernels to dedicated pool this morning (canary=prod-dedicated-1). Running nightly evals now and seeing a non-trivial quality regression on the structured-output suite.
Sam Ortiz: ouch. numbers?
Maya Chen: quick snapshot: mt-bench (structured) avg BLEU down 4.2 pts, hallucination rate +3.1% on our halluc testset. Latency improved ~18% on tail but token-latency variance up.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment prod-dedicated-1 completed at 2025-10-01T09:12:31Z (build 2025.10.1-int8).
Priya Nair: Did we change calibration or quant config for that rollout? static vs dynamic?
Maya Chen: We switched to per-tensor int8 with post-training static calibration (calib set = 2k samples, default histogram bins). Previously fp16.
Carlos Gomez: Could be calibration saturation on a few heads/layers -> breaking structured outputs. Also check kernel selection fallback: small-batch path might use a different int8 kernel with precision tradeoffs.
Jenna Li: Can you paste the profiler traces? pprof and a small nv/cupti snippet would help.
Maya Chen: pasted excerpts:
```
# pprof summary (token-level)
net/forward  64%  (was 55% in fp16)
quant/kernels 18%  (new)
kv/cache-lookup  9%  (increased variance)
```
And a couple of logs from eval run:
```
[WARN] layer 23 activations clipped at 3.2 (calib qparam=0.312)
[INFO] selected kernel int8_gemm_v2_small_batch for seq<=32
[ERROR] structured-serializer mismatch on field 'items[0].price' -> got 'N/A'
```
Sam Ortiz: that kernel selection line is interesting. eng-runtime batching heuristics might be routing many requests to the small-batch int8 kernel which has different accumulation/rounding.
Alex Brooks: I reproduced locally on a 4-GPU dev rig. If I pin kernel to int8_gemm_v1 (legacy) the structured failures drop by ~70% but latency regresses. So it's a correctness/precision vs perf tradeoff.
Priya Nair: Calibration might not be capturing rare activation tails used by structured outputs (format tokens). We should try: 1) enlarge calib set with focused structured-output prompts 2) per-channel scales for problematic layers 3) exclude layernorm/softmax from quant.
Carlos Gomez: Also look at KV cache indexing: int8 kernels changed the key packing order in the runtime optimization. If cache lookup returns slightly different FP results, the serializer might get different tokens. Check off-by-one in kv offsets.
Jenna Li: I ran eval with per-channel int8 and kept layernorm fp16: hallucination delta goes to +0.7% (from +3.1%). BLEU drop reduces to 0.8 pts. That's promising.
Maya Chen: quick test results here:
```
baseline (fp16): BLEU 32.1, halluc 2.3%
int8 static (default): BLEU 27.9, halluc 5.4%
int8 per-channel + ln-fp16: BLEU 31.3, halluc 3.0%
int8 + kernel=v1: BLEU 30.7, halluc 2.6%
```
Sam Ortiz: So we have multiple contributors: quant calibration + per-tensor scaling granularity + kernel selection + KV subtlety. Need to triage order.
Alex Brooks: Repro steps I used:
```
python eval.py --model yoda-7b --quant int8 --calib-file calib_struct.json --kernel auto --batch 8 --seq 64
# try --kernel=int8_gemm_v1 to repro mitigation
```
Priya Nair: Action plan suggestion:
- Rollback canary to fp16 in prod-dedicated-1 (safety)
- Add focused calibration samples covering structured-output prompt varieties
- Add runtime guard: if kernel=int8_gemm_v2 and structured-output route detected, fallback to v1 or ln-fp16 per-layer
- Capture per-layer scale hist during calibration to detect saturation
- Create perf benchmark to measure latency cost of v1 vs v2 at target QPS

Maya Chen: Agree. I'll trigger rollback now.
deploy-bot: Rolling back canary prod-dedicated-1 to build 2025.9.9-fp16 at 2025-10-01T09:32:12Z.
Carlos Gomez: I'll instrument calibration harness to emit per-layer quantization KL/divergence and run a focused 10k-sample calibration pass.
Jenna Li: I'll prototype a runtime kernel-policy flag: prefer precision for 'serializer' routes. Small change in routing table and a unit test.
Sam Ortiz: I'll open a perf/regressions issue and link compiled traces. Tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml, and qa.
Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll post full eval artifacts (calib histograms, token diffs, kv checksums) in this thread once uploaded.
Alex Brooks: quick note — add unit tests that assert deterministic KV hash after quant change. That caught a bug last time.
Maya Chen: uploaded artifacts: link to S3 (s3://redwood-ci/quant-triage/1749001234/).
Sam Ortiz: OK next steps set. Assigning owners: Maya (triage lead), Carlos (calibration), Jenna (runtime fallback), Priya (eval), Alex (unit tests).
Maya Chen: will follow up with a short RFC for safe quant rollout policy (calib thresholds + perf/quality gates).
